title: Samsung Conditions HBM Supply on AMD Foundry Orders

tickers.name: SK hynix Inc. American Depositary Shares

summary:
A senior semiconductor industry official reports that AMD views the use of Samsung Electronics' fabrication plants as too risky for its manufacturing needs. This assessment creates a gap in negotiations, according to Korean media, which state that Samsung is conditioning the supply of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and other components on AMD placing new orders with Samsung Foundry. The discussions in Seoul were intended to find common ground as AMD requires a stable supply of memory to support its AI processors.

CEO Lisa Su met with the head of Samsung's semiconductor business on Wednesday to discuss potential alignment in compute-memory integration. Su previously noted that Samsung and SK Hynix provide critical support for the HBM used in AMD chips and confirmed that the company continues to explore broader collaborations in the memory and foundry sectors.

selectedTweets.text:
According to Korean media reports, Samsung and AMD met today to find common ground: Samsung wants AMD to place orders with Samsung Foundry in return for supplying HBM and other memory, and AMD urgently needs memory.

A senior semiconductor industry official quoted by Korean media said, "AMD sees entrusting its foundry work to Samsung Electronics as too risky," adding, "To secure a stable supply of HBM, AMD has to accept Samsung's proposal, but the two sides see it differently, and that gap is what brought about these talks."
